definitions.meaning: the amount of room something takes up is its capacity or bulk
a single bound tome, especially one of a set

explanation.definitionFit: Volume is both the cubic room a thing fills and one tome of a series.

definitions.meaning: as in the idiom 'dead as a ...', meaning utterly without life
a fastener hammered into a door's woodwork

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'dead as a doornail' gives the lifeless sense; the literal sense is a nail studding a door panel.

definitions.meaning: the aristocratic title of Edgar Rice Burroughs's jungle hero
the jungle hero travels by swinging on vines

explanation.definitionFit: Burroughs's jungle hero is by birth the heir to the Greystoke title and famously swings through trees on lianas.

parts.note: read as the physical measure of how compact or heavy a substance is, mass per unit volume

explanation.definitionFit: In physics, mass per unit volume measures how compact a material is, its thickness of substance.

clue.text: Irish-type collar arranged in such an archaic fashion

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put into a new order, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned Irish collar has been laid out in a museum display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals that the fifteen letters of IRISH-TYPE COLLAR are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a manner from before recorded history is done in an extremely ancient way.

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sort again, so the letters of the French town's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting near to a seaside holiday town in Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place to match the Breton seaside town, but read as 're-sort' it signals rearranging ST MALO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly reaching something is the same as coming close to it, as in 'almost there'.

clue.text: Top Wimbledon player said to give up

indicators.note: said tells us the word is spoken, so we want its sound-alike

parts.note: a leading tennis player is ranked as a seed in the draw

explanation.surface: A leading tennis player at Wimbledon is reported to have surrendered a match.
explanation.walkthrough: At Wimbledon the best players are seeded; SEED sounds just like CEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or hand over territory or a point is to yield it.

clue.text: This bird dead, with nothing to follow? You can say that again!

indicators.note: the exclamation is taken literally: say the little two-letter piece a second time

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An exclamation of emphatic agreement about a bird that is dead and has nothing after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can say that again!' normally means hearty agreement; here it means repeat D+O. The bird is also proverbially dead, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird of Mauritius is the classic example of a vanished species.

definitions.meaning: the single pip on a playing card or die
an outstanding expert or star performer

explanation.definitionFit: The one-pip card is the single spot, and a top performer is a crack expert.

definitions.meaning: sculpture carved so that figures project from a background

explanation.definitionFit: Easing of distress cheers someone; a carving projecting from a flat ground is a raised sculpture.

clue.text: Two-pint measures, you say, and a mineral?

indicators.note: you say signals that the spoken form of the word is what counts

parts.note: a quart is two pints, so these are quarts

explanation.surface: A question about whether liquid measures and a rock sample are connected.
explanation.walkthrough: A quart is two pints in British and US measure; QUARTS sounds like QUARTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystalline silica is a common rock-forming mineral.

parts.note: the main is the high sea, so a seagoing sailing ship; also a tall glass for sherry

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship and a large sherry glass.

clue.text: Taking all the attraction out of a bar perhaps

definitions.text: Taking all the attraction out of a bar perhaps

parts.words: Taking all the attraction out of a bar perhaps
parts.note: read as removing the pull of a bar magnet, not making a pub dull

explanation.definitionFit: Removing magnetism from an iron bar leaves it without its pulling force.

clue.text: What can be done for the poet?

definitions.text: What can be done for the poet?

parts.words: What can be done for the poet?
parts.note: something done is finished or over, and a poet contracts that word for metre

explanation.definitionFit: Poets shorten 'over', meaning finished or done, to a single syllable with an apostrophe.

parts.note: a well is a source of water, a spring
a machine that is not working is switched off

explanation.surface: A toilet whose cistern is fed by a spring that has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flush' suggests plumbing, but it means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having plenty of money, that is, wealthy.

indicators.note: deranged means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Extreme old age drives a person mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An immensely long stretch of time is an aeon, here in its shorter spelling.
A going firm is a commercial enterprise; anxiety about something is also this word.

clue.text: Name in credit as thriller writer

indicators.note: in places the word for name inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a handle is slang for a name or nickname

explanation.surface: A name appearing in the credits of a film written by a crime novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' is not a person's name but its slang synonym, a handle; 'credit' is the bookkeeping abbreviation. Raymond Chandler wrote hard-boiled thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler, creator of Philip Marlowe, was a celebrated author of crime thrillers.

definitions.meaning: the concentrated extract of a substance
the French word for petrol, the fuel French motorists use

explanation.definitionFit: A concentrated extract is a spirit; in France motorists fill their tanks with petrol by this name.

clue.text: Working at Chopin studies, un tutored

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A pianist without lessons is labouring at Chopin's études.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' signals rearranging AT CHOPIN STUDIES. The definition is printed as two words but means untutored.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untaught lacks refinement, being naive and unworldly.

parts.note: O is a short abbreviation for the US state of Ohio
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Fruit from the mountains of Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus fruit is a type of fruit.

clue.text: Muddled clue I would give for mathematician

indicators.note: muddled means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Someone confused by a crossword clue would hand it to a maths expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid of Alexandria was the ancient Greek geometer behind the Elements.

clue.text: Ascend, like one on commercial flight?

definitions.meaning: a moving stairway in a store is a commercial flight of stairs, and riding one you go up

explanation.definitionFit: To rise step by step is to climb, the way a shop's moving staircase carries its riders.

definitions.meaning: a close catching position beside the wicketkeeper in cricket, and its player

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips stand beside the wicketkeeper to catch edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket catching position names its fielder, and a minor error is also this word.

parts.note: snow is slang for cocaine, so a fan of it is a user hooked on the drug

explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependent on cocaine, slangily called snow, is a drug user hooked on it.

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are twisted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish town's awkward stretch of running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges ELGINS; Elgin is a Scottish town. In cricket a single is one run.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket one run scored by the batsmen is a one, so a run equals this.

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A mountain route that is solid and lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is the low saddle between peaks, used as a pass through mountains.

clue.text: Big production seen in the picture-palace?

indicators.note: seen in tells us the letters are visible inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A blockbuster film being shown at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: A picture-palace is an old word for a cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish, large-scale film is called an epic.
